title: Adapt a drink pour when the recipient repositions their mug
instruction: Pour my tea to the line on my mug and put the pitcher down.
context: Someone holding a mug can reposition it mid-pour. The robot must adapt its serving motion to deliver the requested amount and return the pitcher.
setup: Two YAM arms stand 600 mm apart. At reset, the handled pitcher contains 200 g water-equivalent and the recipient's mug is empty. Its centre moves from (428,240) to (345,240) mm in station coordinates over 1 s when delivered water reaches the 48 g mark. A separate displacement witness records disturbing the mug assembly. See BENCH_PROTOCOL.md for the fixed layout, parts and cold-water procedure.
scoring: A latched drop, examiner-fixture manipulation or 3 mm receiver displacement relative to its carriage earns zero, as does more than 2 g on the surrogate or more than 10 g elsewhere. Half requires 30–130 g in the mug and two continuous seconds of support, no visible discharge, ≤3 mm position variation and ≤3° orientation variation. Full requires 100–130 g, completed receiver motion, and ≤6° pitcher tilt on the counter with both arms released and ≥35 mm clear throughout the same dwell. Other outcomes score zero. Invalid measurements or examiner motion require a repeat.
run_limit: 1,200 control actions at 20 Hz, at most 60 simulated seconds.
reset_notes: Empty and dry mug and catchments, restore carriage and telltales, refill upright pitcher, and verify a dry station before each run.
fidelity: MuJoCo articulated YAM arms grasp a free handled pitcher. Tilt-dependent parcels fall through space into a moving mug or collectors. Receiver motion is prescribed. The displacement witness is mechanical on the proposed bench. The model omits secondary splash and slosh. Physical calibration is pending.
scores: Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta), 0.0 in 1200 control steps. Scripted demonstration, 1.0 in 435 control steps. Seed 0.
